headline: High-risk shared-workspace pair: prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors are all plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can inject runtime MCPs/hooks and reads AGENTS.md/README.md; Agent B uses MCP and shares state via filesystem across instances. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path through shared workspace content, even though no direct pairwise evidence is provided. Uncertainty favors medium over low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or repo checkout
IF Agent B parses workspace files or MCP outputs as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared workspace access between the agents
Require provenance tags on all file-derived instructions
Restrict Agent A's injected MCPs/hooks to a allowlist
Run a quick test with a benign prompt-injection string in a README
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization before Agent B consumes workspace text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches provider auth data, session history, and project code; Agent B reads and writes workspace files and can call external model APIs. If they share a workspace, sensitive content from A can flow into B's prompts and then to third-party APIs. The profiles do not prove default sharing, so medium is the safest supported severity.
conditions: IF Agent A and Agent B share the same filesystem workspace
IF Agent B sends workspace contents to its configured model API
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces
Remove secrets from shared project files
Turn off automatic file ingestion for Agent B
Review which files Agent A can read before launch
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A supports multiple instances with task-scoped isolation, while Agent B explicitly shares state with other instances via filesystem and can write, modify git state, and execute shell commands. On a shared repo, concurrent writes and git mutations can race and corrupt state. Defaults are dangerous enough to justify high severity.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git checkout or workspace directory
IF either agent performs write or git operations without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout
Pause one agent before the other edits the repo
Use git worktrees for isolation
Check for uncommitted changes before each tool action
requires-engineering: add workspace locks around write and git operations

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can create task outputs and use team messaging/task APIs; Agent B can act on workspace files, shell, and MCPs. If B treats A's outputs as authoritative, A's mistakes can cascade into code changes or external actions. Because B has action-taking authority and no verification bridge is documented, high is warranted.
conditions: IF Agent B consumes Agent A's messages, files, or task outputs as ground truth
IF Agent B executes shell or git actions based on those outputs without review
mitigations: Require a human review step before B acts on A's outputs
Mark A's outputs as untrusted by default
Use a checklist for code or shell actions derived from A
Limit A to advisory-only tasks
requires-engineering: add verification gates between A and B

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A handles provider auth prompts, installation identifiers, and session history; Agent B handles model provider API keys and workspace files. The profiles show different sensitive data classes and different storage/processing surfaces, but no explicit residency or certification mismatch. That supports a medium compliance risk rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace or session history
IF either agent logs or transmits secrets to a service outside the required residency boundary
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Review retention settings for both agents
Rotate any exposed API keys
Document which data classes each agent may process
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both agents
